title: A Calculator for Statin Side-Effect Worry
hook: A new Oxford calculator predicts your personal risk of serious statin muscle problems — and finds over 98% of eligible people are actually at low risk.
key_points: Oxford researchers built a calculator estimating a person's individual risk of serious statin-related muscle disorders.
More than 98% of people who qualify for statins were found to be at low risk for these rare complications.
Despite this, the analysis found many eligible people aren't taking statins.
That gap means missed protection against heart attacks and strokes for people who could benefit.
content_html: Fear of muscle pain and other side effects keeps many people who could benefit from statins from taking them. A new calculator built by University of Oxford researchers aims to cut through that fear with individualized numbers: according to ScienceDaily, their analysis found that more than 98% of people who qualify for statins are actually at low risk for serious muscle complications.
extra_html: The flip side of the finding is what makes it matter: despite that reassuring risk profile, the study found most eligible patients still aren't taking statins — potentially missing out on real protection against heart attacks and strokes. The calculator is designed to give people a personalized risk estimate instead of a vague, one-size-fits-all warning, so the decision to start or stick with a statin can be based on their actual odds rather than general side-effect anxiety. As always, whether to start one is a conversation to have with your own clinician.

related.title: Understanding Cholesterol
related.hook: Cholesterol has a good side and a bad side. Too much of the bad kind builds up in your arteries for years — silently — until it triggers a heart attack or stroke.

flashcards.prompt: What did the Oxford calculator find about statin muscle-side-effect risk for most eligible people?
flashcards.back_html: More than 98% of people who qualify for statins were at low risk for serious muscle disorders — despite widespread concern about side effects.

flashcards.prompt: What's the practical consequence of many eligible people avoiding statins over side-effect fears?

choices.text: They may be missing meaningful protection against heart attacks and strokes
They automatically develop worse muscle disorders instead
There is no consequence — statins provide no real benefit
